title: Debating Ethical Dilemmas / Débat ci suuf yu bare
bridge: Bés bu yàgg ci wóolor ci suuf, yi ngi jàpp ci subjonctif ci ñeexal ci opinion. Bés bu Tool, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, ndax subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir. Subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir. Subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir. Subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir. Subjonctif a maaj ci mbir, subjonctif a maaj ci mbir.
rule: Bés bu Tool ci B2, ndaxte ci suuf, yi ngi jàpp ci: 1) 'I think/ believe/ feel' + clause ci indicatif: 'I think that...' (subjonctif a maaj ci mbir). 2) Modals: 'should' (recommandation), 'ought to' (formal), 'must' (obligation forte), 'can't' (impossibilité), 'could' (possibilité), 'would' (hypothèse). 3) Structures ci accord/désaccord: 'I agree with... because...', 'I see your point, but...', 'That may be true, however...'. 4) Conditional ci hypothèse éthique: 'If we allowed... , then...' (premier conditionnel), 'If I were in that situation, I would...' (deuxième conditionnel). 5) Connecteurs: 'therefore', 'moreover', 'nevertheless', 'although'. Dafa doxal ci négation double ('I don't agree with nothing' a maaj ci mbir) ndaxte ci suuf, yi ngi jàpp ci inversion ci enfatizar: 'Not only is it unethical, but also...'.

concept_examples.text: I believe that animal testing is unethical because it causes unnecessary suffering.
concept_examples.translation: Mën naa ngi wax ci suuf nekk ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ bɪˈliːv ðæt ˈænɪməl ˈtestɪŋ ɪz ʌnˈeθɪkəl bɪˈkɔːz ɪt ˈkɔːzɪz ʌnˈnesəseri ˈsʌfərɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: If I were in that situation, I would tell the truth, even if it was difficult.

concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wɜːr ɪn ðæt ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən, aɪ wʊd tɛl ðə truːθ, ˈiːvən ɪf ɪt wʌz ˈdɪfɪkəlt/

concept_examples.text: Some people argue that genetically modified crops are necessary to feed the world, but others disagree.
concept_examples.translation: Ci suuf yi ngi wax ci suuf nekk ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sʌm ˈpiːpəl ˈɑːrɡjuː ðæt dʒəˈnetɪkli ˈmɒdɪfaɪd krɒps ɑːr ˈnesəseri tuː fiːd ðə wɜːrld, bʌt ˈʌðərz ˌdɪsəˈɡriː/

concept_examples.text: We shouldn't sacrifice privacy for security; both are essential.
concept_examples.translation: Dafa doxal ci négation double ('No creo que no sea ético'), ndaxte ci suuf, yi ngi jàpp ci reformuler ci laa nekk ci suuf.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ˈʃʊdnt ˈsækrɪfaɪs ˈpraɪvəsi fɔːr sɪˈkjʊrəti; boʊθ ɑːr ɪˈsenʃəl/

common_error.wrong: I don't think that it is not ethical to lie.
common_error.correct: I don't think it is ethical to lie.
common_error.correct_alt: I think it is unethical to lie.
common_error.explanation: L'erreur se produit parce qu'en espagnol, la double négation est courante ('No creo que no sea ético'), mais en anglais, une phrase ne peut avoir qu'une seule négation principale. Pour corriger, supprimez le 'not' supplémentaire ou reformulez avec le mot opposé (unethical).

examples.original: In my opinion, we should recycle more.

examples.note: Usa 'in my opinion' al inicio para enfatizar tu punto de vista.

examples.original: I strongly believe that every child deserves a quality education.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈstrɔŋli bɪˈliːv ðæt ˈɛvri tʃaɪld dɪˈzɜːrvz ə ˈkwɒləti ˌɛdʒuˈkeɪʃən/

examples.note: El adverbio 'strongly' va antes del verbo principal 'believe'.

examples.original: From my perspective, this policy has more benefits than drawbacks.
examples.phonetic: /frɒm maɪ pərˈspɛktɪv, ðɪs ˈpɒləsi hæz mɔːr ˈbɛnɪfɪts ðæn ˈdrɔːbæks/

examples.note: Evita traducir literalmente 'Bajo mi punto de vista'.

examples.original: I couldn't agree more with your argument about renewable energy.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈkʊdnt əˈɡriː mɔːr wɪð jɔːr ˈɑːrɡjumənt əˈbaʊt rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈɛnərdʒi/
examples.translation: Dafa doxal ci négation double ('I can't agree with your argument about renewable energy.' a maaj ci mbir).
examples.note: Esta expresión significa un acuerdo total. No la confundas con 'I can't agree' (no estoy de acuerdo).

examples.original: I see your point, but I think there are other factors to consider.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ siː jɔːr pɔɪnt, bʌt aɪ θɪŋk ðeər ɑːr ˈʌðər ˈfæktərz tuː kənˈsɪdər/
examples.translation: Mën naa ngi wax ci suuf nekk ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf.
examples.note: Forma cortés de discrepar sin ofender.

examples.original: That may be true, however, we must also think about the long-term effects.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt meɪ biː truː, haʊˈɛvər, wiː mʌst ˈɔːlsoʊ θɪŋk əˈbaʊt ðə ˈlɔːŋtɜːrm ɪˈfɛkts/
examples.translation: Dafa doxal ci négation double ('That may be true, however, we must also think about the long-term effects.' a maaj ci mbir).
examples.note: El uso de 'however' después de una pausa con coma.

examples.original: If the government banned all private cars, the air quality would improve significantly.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ðə ˈɡʌvərnmənt bænd ɔːl ˈpraɪvɪt kɑːrz, ðiː ɛər ˈkwɒləti wʊd ɪmˈpruːv sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/
examples.translation: Su gouvernementu teewul ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf.
examples.note: Segundo condicional para situaciones improbables o hipotéticas. En inglés, usa 'were' en lugar de 'was' para todos los sujetos en el condicional.

examples.original: If I were the CEO, I would prioritize employee well-being over profits.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wɜːr ðə ˌsiː.iːˈoʊ, aɪ wʊd praɪˈɔːrɪtaɪz ˌɛmplɔɪˈiː ˌwɛlˈbiːɪŋ ˈoʊvər ˈprɒfɪts/
examples.translation: Su maa ko wax ci suuf nekk ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf.
examples.note: Uso correcto de 'were' en el subjuntivo pasado. La mayoría de los hablantes de español tienden a decir 'I was'.

examples.original: What would you do if you found a wallet with a thousand dollars inside?
examples.phonetic: /wʌt wʊd juː duː ɪf juː faʊnd ə ˈwɔːlɪt wɪð ə ˈθaʊzənd ˈdɒlərz ɪnˈsaɪd?/
examples.translation: Lan laa ko wax ci suuf nekk ci suuf yu bare laa nekk ci suuf?

examples.original: If we don't act now, future generations will suffer the consequences.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wiː doʊnt ækt naʊ, ˈfjuːtʃər ˌdʒɛnəˈreɪʃənz wɪl ˈsʌfər ðə ˈkɒnsɪkwɛnsɪz/

examples.note: Primer condicional para situaciones reales y probables.

title: Strategic Language for Negotiations / Ndimmal ci mbiralekat
bridge: In Wolof, we often use polite expressions like 'maangi fi' or 'maangi laa ci' to sound courteous, similar to how Spanish uses the subjunctive ('quisiera', 'me gustaría'). In English, modals like 'would', 'could', and 'might' serve the same purpose but with a different structure. Wolof speakers may also be more direct when rejecting an offer, while English expects softened refusals like 'I'm afraid' or 'unfortunately'. Be careful not to translate 'de acuerdo' literally as 'maangi laa ci'—the correct verb is 'di naa' without the auxiliary.
rule: In B2-level English negotiations, modals are used to express politeness and nuances (would, could, might, may). Structures like 'I would suggest...' or 'We could consider...' are preferred over 'I want...' or 'You must...'. For counterproposals, 'What if...' or 'How about...' followed by a gerund or clause are used. To diplomatically express disagreement, attenuators like 'I see your point, but...' or 'I'm afraid that...' are employed. When negotiating terms, conditionals (If... then...) are used. Remember that in English, 'agree' is a verb, not an adjective, so it is not said 'I am agree' but 'I agree'.

concept_examples.text: I would suggest we postpone the deadline to next week.
concept_examples.translation: Maangi laa ci fi ma ngir def ci ndimmal.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd səˈdʒɛst wi poʊstˈpoʊn ðə ˈdɛdlaɪn tu nɛkst wik/

concept_examples.text: We could consider a discount if you increase the order volume.
concept_examples.translation: Nungi ko ci mbiralekat maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wi kʊd kənˈsɪdər ə ˈdɪskaʊnt ɪf ju ˈɪnkris ðə ˈɔrdər ˈvɑljum/

concept_examples.text: I'm afraid that price is a bit higher than we expected.
concept_examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir ci mbiralekat.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪm əˈfreɪd ðæt praɪs ɪz ə bɪt ˈhaɪər ðæn wi ɪkˈspɛktɪd/

concept_examples.text: What if we split the difference and meet in the middle?
concept_examples.translation: Lu maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci mbiralekat?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wʌt ɪf wi splɪt ðə ˈdɪfərəns ænd mit ɪn ðə ˈmɪdəl/

common_error.wrong: I am agree with your proposal, but we need a better price.
common_error.correct: I agree with your proposal, but we need a better price.
common_error.correct_alt: I completely agree with your proposal, but we would need a better price.
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Spanish, 'estoy de acuerdo' (using the verb 'estar' + noun) is literally translated to English as 'I am agree'. In English, 'agree' is a full verb, not an adjective, so it is not used with 'to be'. To avoid this error, remember that 'agree' functions like 'coincide' or 'be in agreement' but without the auxiliary 'be'. Adverbs like 'completely' or 'partially' can also be used to soften the agreement.

examples.original: I would like to propose a different approach.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tə prəˈpoʊz ə ˈdɪfərənt əˈproʊtʃ/
examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal.
examples.note: Use 'would like to' to sound formal and polite, equivalent to 'quisiera' in Spanish but without the subjunctive.

examples.original: How about meeting next Tuesday?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ˈmitɪŋ nɛkst ˈtuzdeɪ/
examples.translation: Lu maangi laa ci ne ma ngir dem ci talaata?
examples.note: 'How about' followed by a gerund is a colloquial way to make a suggestion. It is not translated literally.

examples.original: I suggest we revisit the terms of the contract.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ səˈdʒɛst wi riˈvɪzɪt ðə tɜrmz əv ðə ˈkɑntrækt/
examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal ci mbiralekat.
examples.note: In English, after 'suggest', the base subjunctive (without 's' in the third person) is used, similar to the Spanish subjunctive.

examples.original: I see your point, but I have some concerns about the timeline.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ si jʊr pɔɪnt bʌt aɪ hæv sʌm kənˈsɜrnz əˈbaʊt ðə ˈtaɪmlaɪn/
examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal ci mbiralekat.
examples.note: This structure softens disagreement by first acknowledging the other person's point.

examples.original: I'm afraid that's not quite what we had in mind.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm əˈfreɪd ðæts nɑt kwaɪt wʌt wi hæd ɪn maɪnd/
examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir ci mbiralekat.
examples.note: 'I'm afraid' does not express fear but a polite rejection. It is a very useful filler phrase.

examples.original: I understand your position, but we would need more flexibility.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˌʌndərˈstænd jʊr pəˈzɪʃən bʌt wi wʊd nid mɔr ˌflɛksəˈbɪlɪti/
examples.translation: Maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal ci mbiralekat.
examples.note: Use 'would need' instead of 'need' to sound more conditional and less demanding.

examples.original: If you can offer a 10% discount, we would be willing to sign today.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju kæn ˈɔfər ə tɛn pɜrˈsɛnt ˈdɪskaʊnt wi wʊd bi ˈwɪlɪŋ tə saɪn təˈdeɪ/
examples.translation: Su ma ngir def ci mbiralekat ci ndimmal, maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal.
examples.note: Conditional with 'if' + 'would' to create a conditional offer.

examples.original: Let's meet halfway on the shipping costs.
examples.phonetic: /lɛts mit ˈhæfweɪ ɒn ðə ˈʃɪpɪŋ kɔsts/
examples.translation: Dama jëf ci mbiralekat ci ndimmal ci mbiralekat.
examples.note: 'Meet halfway' is an idiomatic expression for reaching a middle-ground agreement.

examples.original: We have a deal if you agree to these terms.
examples.phonetic: /wi hæv ə dil ɪf ju əˈgri tə ðiz tɜrmz/
examples.translation: Nungi ci mbiralekat maangi laa ci ne ma ngir jëf ci ndimmal.
examples.note: 'A deal' is used instead of 'an agreement' in casual negotiation contexts.
